A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PASR research. All 23 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, token-consumption measurements, ablations, and refinement-behavior analyses, including additional experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark evaluations and appendix experiments, alongside ablations and analyses of refinement behavior.

M1.justification: PASR retains GRPO training, nested think/refine/answer tags, and the same format, accuracy, and comparison-based refinement rewards. Rewritten action descriptions and rollout explanations do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same filtered instruction-training corpus and ten evaluation datasets covering mathematics, reasoning, knowledge, and summarization. The appendix examples and represented tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: Vanilla, Self-Refine, Self-Refine+, PTR, SCoRe, STaR, ISC, RISE where originally included, and the PASR prompting and instruction-tuning variants. Changed baseline scores do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The reported backbone configurations, training settings, evaluation metrics, and analysis sample sizes remain unchanged. Missing documentation about the reward-ablation backbone and altered template formatting do not establish a changed experimental procedure.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the prompting/instruction-tuning comparisons, two reward ablations, refinement-timing and coherence/alignment analyses, refinement-type statistics, and failure-case analysis. The four appendix examples are reformatted rather than replaced.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains identical refinement-type proportions and 95% Wilson confidence intervals. Repeated scoring of the 300 refinement samples is also retained, without new seed counts, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: In Table 1, Qwen2.5-7B AIME24 scores for Vanilla and Self-Refine+ change from 16.7 to 6.7; their averages change from 56.9 to 55.9 and 63.3 to 62.3, respectively. PASR scores and Tables 2–3 remain unchanged. Figure 3 also adds an average-token axis to the Qwen2.5-7B radar.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation and optimization and reward definitions in Equations (1)–(7) retain their mathematical substance. Trace-action descriptions replace some indexing notation with explanatory prose; no new assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The introduction removes v1's explicit claim to be the first to propose proactive self-refinement as a formal task. The central PASR contributions and headline Qwen3-8B claims of 41.6% fewer tokens and 8.2% higher accuracy remain.

C2.justification: V2 removes Appendix D's specific acknowledgment that trajectory evaluation relies on subjective LLM judgments and lacks objective, reliable metrics. This qualification is not relocated. Appendix B retains the limitations concerning knowledge gaps and inadequate metacognitive ability.

D1.justification: V2 drops the explicit Qwen2.5-7B backbone specification for the reward ablation. Its displayed summary and multiple-choice evaluation templates also lose their question placeholders. Hardware, hyperparameters, training-data preparation, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged; these are documentation changes.

R1.justification: The introduction now acknowledges in-process refinement in DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI-o1 rather than emphasizing superficial refinement and over/underthinking. V2 adds the o1 system-card citation and removes several planning, judging, and thinking-related references. The broader positioning against post-hoc refinement remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and substantial portions of the GRPO, rollout, and reward explanations are rewritten and condensed. Contributions become bullets, Sections 3.3.1–3.3.2 become Sections 3.3–3.4, and appendix organization changes. Distinct prompt references are replaced by confusing Table/Figure B.3 references.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a larger three-panel illustration on page 2. Figures 3–4 are redrawn, including revised radar scales and an added average axis. Table 2 becomes single-column. Numerous separately captioned appendix figures become multipage boxes, splitting examples and prompts and leaving substantial blank areas.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition and the enlarged Figure 1 are offset by reduced reporting transparency and consistency. V2 removes the specific trajectory-evaluation limitations and changes Table 1 so that 61.7 minus 55.9 implies a 5.8-point gain, while retaining the 4.8-point claim. Lost template details and confusing appendix references further reduce usability. The core method and experimental evidence remain largely intact, limiting the overall deterioration.
